definitions.explanation: A privately owned agricultural estate in pre-modern Japan, particularly from the Nara through Muromachi periods. Manors were granted tax-exempt status and were controlled by aristocrats, temples, or shrines. Composed of 荘 (estate) + 園 (land).

examples.japanese: {平安時代|へいあんじだい}には{荘園|しょうえん}が{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: Manors increased during the Heian period.

examples.japanese: {貴族|きぞく}たちは{広大|こうだい}な{荘園|しょうえん}を{所有|しょゆう}していた。
examples.english: The aristocrats owned vast manorial estates.

examples.japanese: {荘園|しょうえん}{制度|せいど}の{崩壊|ほうかい}は{武士|ぶし}の{台頭|たいとう}と{深|ふか}く{関|かか}わっている。
examples.english: The collapse of the manor system is deeply connected to the rise of the warrior class.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The {荘園|しょうえん} system developed in Japan from the 8th century onward. Powerful families, temples, and shrines accumulated tax-exempt lands, weakening central government revenue. The system gradually declined as warrior clans gained control of the land during the Kamakura and Muromachi periods.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {荘園|しょうえん}{制度|せいど} (manorial system)
- {荘園|しょうえん}{領主|りょうしゅ} (manor lord)
- {荘園|しょうえん}を{管理|かんり}する (to manage a manor)
- {荘園|しょうえん}の{整理|せいり} (reorganization of manors — historical reform efforts)
